latest_nl_proof:
Fix an integer n>1 and a real number t with (n-1)/n <= t < 1. Let k be any integer with 1 <= k <= n. We show that floor(k t) = k-1.

From t < 1 we get k t < k.
From t >= (n-1)/n we get
k t >= k(n-1)/n = k - k/n.
Since k <= n, we have k/n <= 1, hence k - k/n >= k - 1. Therefore
k - 1 <= k t < k.

Because k-1 is an integer and it is the greatest integer not exceeding k t, it follows that floor(k t) = k-1.

Since k was arbitrary, this holds for every integer k with 1 <= k <= n.
